ensemble.source: Hausfather, The Climate Brink -- multi-model synthesis (NMME + C3S + SINTEX-F)
ensemble.peak_p90_note: Upper bound is not published as a discrete figure; the source states the middle 80% of members spans 2.8 degC to above 3.6 degC. 4.4 is a symmetric-tail reconstruction and is rendered as an open-ended band.
ensemble.verification_caveat: No El Nino of this amplitude exists in the observational record. Model skill above roughly 3 degC in Nino 3.4 is unverified by construction.

countries.name: Peru
countries.notes: Dual-signed, and the national figure understates both halves. Coastal north (Piura, Lambayeque, Tumbes) can see several times normal rainfall -- 1997-98 delivered order-of-magnitude departures there -- while the southern Andean altiplano dries, hitting potato and quinoa. The value shown is a national DJF mean; read the coastal hazard, not the average. Anchoveta biomass is the single most El-Nino-elastic commodity series on the planet.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.notes: Strongest and most reliable dry teleconnection globally. Sumatra and Kalimantan peat fires drive haze events; 2015-16 analogue burned ~2.6 Mha. Palm oil yield response lags rainfall deficit by 6-12 months, so the production hit lands mostly in 2027.

countries.name: Australia
countries.notes: Eastern and northern Australia dry. Wheat belt response is concentrated in the Sep-Nov grain fill window, so the 2026-27 hit shows up in the 2026-27 harvest already, ahead of the SST peak.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.notes: Oct-Dec short rains enhanced. Net effect on maize is positive-to-neutral; the dominant risks are flood displacement and vector-borne disease. Tea and coffee quality can suffer from excess moisture.

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.notes: Split signal: Jun-Sep kiremt rains suppressed (main crop), Oct-Dec enhanced. The kiremt deficit dominates the cereal balance. Arabica coffee origin risk is material.

countries.name: India
countries.notes: The critical window is the JJAS southwest monsoon of 2027, i.e. AFTER the SST peak, when El Nino decay-year monsoons are historically weakest. Indian rice export policy is the largest single swing factor in the global rice price complex.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.notes: Central Highlands robusta is the exposure that matters most for world coffee. Mekong Delta salinity intrusion compounds the rice signal.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.notes: Strongly dipolar. North and northeast dry (Amazon drought, record fire risk peaking H2 2027); south (Rio Grande do Sul, Parana) wet, which helps soy but raises harvest-quality and logistics risk. Arabica in Minas Gerais sits near the transition line -- the highest-variance call on the board.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.notes: Historically the clearest El Nino *beneficiary* in row crops. Wetter pampas typically lifts soy and maize yields, partially offsetting losses elsewhere. This is the main reason a global grain price shock is not a foregone conclusion.

countries.name: United States
countries.notes: Wet southern tier (California to Florida), warm and dry north. Winter wheat in the southern Plains typically benefits. Suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity is a meaningful positive for Gulf energy and agricultural logistics.

countries.name: Cote d'Ivoire
countries.notes: West African cocoa has a weak and inconsistent ENSO teleconnection -- confidence is deliberately low. Harmattan intensity is the transmission channel most often cited, but the composite barely clears noise.

market_baseline.source: Helios AI palm oil outlook, July 2026

escalations.name: Peru
escalations.notes: Dual-signed, and the national figure understates both halves. Coastal north (Piura, Lambayeque, Tumbes) can see several times normal rainfall -- 1997-98 delivered order-of-magnitude departures there -- while the southern Andean altiplano dries, hitting potato and quinoa. The value shown is a national DJF mean; read the coastal hazard, not the average. Anchoveta biomass is the single most El-Nino-elastic commodity series on the planet.

ONI.note: The headline measure of El Nino strength: a 3-month running mean of sea surface temperature anomaly in the Nino 3.4 region, measured against a 30-year climatology that shifts every five years.

CPC.note: The US agency that declares official El Nino / La Nina status and publishes the ONI table this dashboard treats as the reference.

Nino 3.4.full: Nino 3.4 region (5 deg N-5 deg S, 170 deg W-120 deg W)
Nino 3.4.note: The central-equatorial Pacific box whose sea surface temperature defines the ONI. Not the only Nino region -- Nino 1+2 sits off the Peruvian coast and responds far more sharply, which is why coastal Peru floods before the headline index looks extreme.

ERSSTv5.full: Extended Reconstructed Sea Surface Temperature, version 5
ERSSTv5.note: The gridded SST dataset underlying both the ONI and the record comparison.

ENSO.note: The coupled ocean-atmosphere cycle of which El Nino is the warm phase.

NMME.note: Six US and Canadian coupled forecast models run as one ensemble.

C3S.note: The European multi-system seasonal forecast, combining seven centres.

ECMWF.full: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts

JAMSTEC.full: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

ERA5.note: Supplies the 1991-2020 baseline the impact layers are measured against.

CHIRPS.full: Climate Hazards Group Infrared Precipitation with Stations

WASDE.full: World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (USDA)

FAO.full: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

GIEWS.full: Global Information and Early Warning System (FAO)

FCPO.full: crude palm oil futures contract (Bursa Malaysia)

FOB.full: free on board (price at port of loading)

IMARPE.note: Runs the anchoveta biomass surveys that set Peru's fishing quota.

SENAMHI.full: Peru's national meteorology and hydrology service

ENFEN.full: Peru's multi-agency El Nino study committee
ENFEN.note: Publishes the coastal El Nino index, which can diverge sharply from the ONI.

BMKG.full: Indonesia's meteorology, climatology and geophysics agency

Confidence.note: How reliable this region's teleconnection is in the historical record, multiplied by a 35% penalty applied while the forecast sits above the amplitude any composite was calibrated on. The penalty is already included in the number shown.

composite.full: a published teleconnection composite, rescaled to forecast intensity
composite.note: The typical response of a region to a strong El Nino, taken from the literature and scaled up. Not dynamically downscaled model output -- the sign is well established, the magnitude at this amplitude is not.

teleconnection.full: a statistical link between Pacific sea surface temperature and distant weather

p10.note: One in ten ensemble members falls below this value.

p90.note: One in ten ensemble members falls above this value.

HHI.note: A supply-concentration measure; higher means fewer countries dominate output.

commodities.title: How to read this table
commodities.method: Price response is not measured; it is derived. The chain is: production shock = sum over countries of (share of world production x that country's yield sensitivity x intensity factor), where the intensity factor is (forecast / 2.4)^0.85 = 1.41 at the current 3.6 degC median -- sub-linear because teleconnection responses saturate. Then price response = -(production shock) x elasticity x stock modifier x thin-market multiplier. A negative shock (lost output) therefore produces a positive price response. Fishmeal is the exception: it routes through a fisheries chain instead, where biomass is modelled as compounding depletion (survival raised to the intensity factor) and then passes through the quota decision and rendering yield.
commodities.caveat: These are scenario outputs, not forecasts. Elasticities are calibrated so that the two El Nino price responses we could attribute to a published source fall inside the modelled band: palm oil +20-40% at a six-month lag, and fishmeal ~+80% on a ~40% production fall. A modelled value that departs from its anchor by more than 2x raises a quality-control flag.

columns.label: Commodity
columns.definition: The traded commodity. Crop and fisheries routes are mixed in one table.

columns.label: Venue
columns.definition: Where the reference price is set. OTC means no central exchange, so the reference is a negotiated port price.

columns.label: Prod. shock %
columns.definition: Modelled change in GLOBAL production, weighted by each country's share of world output. Negative is lost supply. Positive values are real: Argentina and southern Brazil gain in an El Nino, which is why soybeans show a surplus.

columns.label: Price response %
columns.definition: Modelled price move at the peak of transmission. Positive means upward pressure. See the method note above for the full chain.

columns.label: Elasticity
columns.definition: Percent price move per 1% of lost global production. Higher means a given shortfall bites harder. Thin, unstocked markets sit above 2.

columns.label: Stock/use
columns.definition: Carryover stocks as a share of annual consumption. Deep stocks absorb a shock; a dash means no meaningful carryover exists, which is why fishmeal transmits so fast.

columns.label: Stock mod.
columns.definition: The multiplier that stock cover applies to elasticity, bounded to [0.70, 1.60]. Deep stocks damp below 1.0; thin stocks amplify above. The bound exists because an earlier unbounded version compounded into a 242% palm-oil response.

columns.label: Modelled
columns.definition: Share of world production this system has an ACTUAL response for. This is the honest denominator -- read the shock as an estimate over this much of the market, not the whole of it.

columns.label: Listed
columns.definition: Share of world production the system can name. The gap between Listed and Modelled is supply known to exist but not modelled -- for fishmeal that is largely Chinese rendering of imported raw material, which does not respond to a Peruvian El Nino.

columns.label: Lag (mo)
columns.definition: Months from the sea-surface temperature peak to the expected price peak. Perennials lag longest; fishmeal is fastest at 3 months.

columns.label: Top 3
columns.definition: The three countries contributing the largest share of the modelled shock, most negative first.

countries.title: How to read this table
countries.method: Every value here is a published teleconnection composite -- the typical response of a region to a strong El Nino -- rescaled to the forecast intensity by a factor of (forecast / 2.4)^0.85 = 1.41. They are composite, not model output: the sign of each response is well established in the literature, the magnitude at this amplitude is not.
countries.caveat: National means hide sub-national extremes. Peru is the clearest case -- the national figure is a fraction of what coastal Piura and Lambayeque experience. Read the hazard list alongside the average.

columns.label: Region
columns.definition: Country, or the modelled region where a country is treated as one unit.

columns.label: Group
columns.definition: Teleconnection grouping, used for ordering rather than for any calculation.

columns.label: Precip DJF %
columns.definition: Rainfall departure for December-February 2026-27, as a percent of the 1991-2020 seasonal total. Negative is drier.

columns.label: Precip MAM %
columns.definition: Same, for March-May 2027 -- the decay-phase season.

columns.label: Temp DJF degC
columns.definition: Temperature departure for December-February against the 1991-2020 mean.

columns.label: Yield index %
columns.definition: Exposure-weighted crop yield deviation across everything the country grows. SIGNED: positive means a yield gain, which several regions genuinely get.

columns.label: Fire/drought
columns.definition: Combined fire and drought load, 0-100, normalised across the modelled set so 100 is the worst region rather than an absolute ceiling. Ranks regions against each other; it is not a probability.

columns.label: Price pressure
columns.definition: 0-100 index of how hard this country's losses push on world prices, weighting its crops by elasticity and stock cover. A country can have a large yield loss and low price pressure if it grows things the world holds stocks of.

columns.label: Fisheries %
columns.definition: Fish biomass anomaly. Peru, Chile and Ecuador only -- blank elsewhere means not modelled, not zero.

columns.label: Confidence
columns.definition: How much weight to put on this row, 0 to 1. It is the product of two things: how RELIABLE the teleconnection is for this region in the historical record, and a penalty for forecasting beyond it.
columns.detail: The base term is a per-region prior. Indonesia scores high (0.91 before penalty) because its dry signal appears in almost every El Nino on record; West African cocoa scores low (0.46-0.48) because the signal there barely clears noise. The second term is a flat 35% penalty applied to EVERY region while the forecast median sits above 2.8 degC, the amplitude beyond which composites have no observational grounding. That penalty is already included in the number shown -- it is not applied again downstream. So 0.52 here means "a reasonably reliable teleconnection, discounted because no event this large has ever been observed", not "a coin flip".

columns.label: Hazards
columns.definition: The specific mechanisms expected in this region. Where a value looks mild, the hazard list often carries the risk the average hides.

literature_anchors._comment: Quantified, citable response magnitudes used to sanity-check the impact model. Any modelled output that departs from these by more than a factor of 2 raises a QC flag.

anchoveta_biomass_1997_98.detail: Peruvian anchoveta biomass fell from 5.8 Mt to a minimum of 1.2 Mt
anchoveta_biomass_1997_98.source: ICES Journal of Marine Science -- phenological mismatch and anchoveta landings

fishmeal_price_response.detail: A ~40% fall in global fishmeal production coincided with an ~80% price rise to an all-time high. Implied elasticity ~2.0, which is what the model uses. Band widened to 60-100% to reflect that this is one episode.
fishmeal_price_response.source: The Week -- the global anchovy crisis

fishmeal_andean_share.detail: Peru, Chile and Ecuador together account for nearly a third of world fishmeal.
fishmeal_andean_share.source: The Week -- the global anchovy crisis

_comment: Figures supplied in the commissioning brief that could NOT be traced to a
primary source during the 2026-07-26 research pass. They are carried here
so they are auditable, and are rendered in the dashboard only inside the
explicitly-labelled scenario band -- never as forecasts. Step A re-attempts
attribution on every run and promotes anything that resolves.

price_shock_rice_palm_coffee_pct.conflict: Exceeds the only sourced El Nino palm price response found (20-40% at 6-month lag) by roughly 2-3x. Flagged as a tail scenario, not a central case.

gmst_2027_above_preindustrial_degC.note: The 'warmest year on record by a sizable margin' framing is directly sourced; the specific 1.8 degC figure is not.
